newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Southcorp confident of profit rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Southcorp confident of profit rise.

text.p: Wine, packaging, and appliance manufacturer Southcorp Holdings Ltd said it was confident of a growth in earnings this financial year, repeating comments made in the past two months since the company reported a 2.5 percent rise in 1995/96 net profit to A$118.2 million.

"In the overall sense, although market conditions for most of our businesses are expected to remain highly competitive, your directors are confident that, provided there is no significant downturn in the Australian and USA economies, there are good prospects for continued growth in earnings," chairman Rick Allert said at the annual meeting.
"The Australian 'manufacturing' economy in which many of Southcorp's businesses operate show little sign of strong economic growth," he said.

"There is no doubt that overall the current business environment is tough and very competitive, and appears likely to continue that way for the remainder of the year. However, the rural recovery in Australia has been positive for our packaging business with increased demand for many of our products."
Allert said the strong U.S. economy was a positive factor for Southcorp's wine and packaging divisions as well as providing solid demand for the water heating operations.

Allert said Southcorp hoped the slump in Australian housing starts had bottomed and he welcomed the recent rise in housing approvals even though this would take up to nine months to become completions. "At this stage we do not expect housing completions to grow until the June quarter of 1997," he said.

The company did not provide a specific net profit forecast for the current year but managing director Graham Kraehe recently told Reuters he was comfortable with analysts forecasts which ranged up to about A$135 million.
